tracking.title: Shooting outside Restaurante Flamas
tracking.status: Murder — victim died; no arrests or suspects reported
tracking.summary: Alejandro Chaparro Ruiz, 66, of Aguada, was shot in the abdomen around 1:24 a.m. on Friday, Nov 20, in front of Restaurante Flamas. He was moved from Hospital Buen Samaritano to Centro Médico in Río Piedras, where he died that day. Police now classify it as a murder. The CIC Aguadilla Homicide Division is investigating; no suspect or arrest has been reported.

timeline.text: Checked again: no suspect, motive or arrest has been reported since Chaparro's death.
body: No follow-up reporting on an arrest, a suspect or a motive turned up in Puerto Rico outlets as of Nov 25.
The CIC Aguadilla Homicide Division is handling the case as a murder.

timeline.text: Chaparro died of his wound after being moved to a San Juan–area hospital. Police now count the case as a murder. Still no suspect or arrest reported.
body: Metro's weekend police summary listed the Flamas shooting as one of three murders in Puerto Rico from Friday, Nov 20, to Sunday, Nov 22, and gave the victim's full name as Alejandro Chaparro Ruiz.

He was first treated at Hospital Buen Samaritano in Aguadilla, then referred to a metro-area hospital, where he died. Periódico La Perla reported he died Friday at Centro Médico in Río Piedras. Earlier reports describing him as stable are out of date.

timeline.text: Police reclassified the shooting as a murder after Chaparro died at Centro Médico in Río Piedras.
body: NotiCel reported that the aggravated-assault case became a murder investigation after Chaparro died of his wounds at Centro Médico in Río Piedras, where he had been referred from Hospital Buen Samaritano.
No suspect or motive was reported.

timeline.text: Victim identified as Alejandro Chaparro, 66, of Aguada. Referred from Buen Samaritano to a metro-area hospital.
body: Police received a 9-1-1 call about a person lying on the pavement in front of a restaurant in barrio Victoria.

Officers found a man with a gunshot wound to the abdomen. Emergency medical crews treated him at the scene and took him to Hospital Buen Samaritano in Aguadilla, where he was referred on to a hospital in the San Juan metro area.

timeline.text: Shot at about 1:24 a.m. in front of Restaurante Flamas; condition stable. Homicide Division investigating.
body: Telemundo placed the shooting at about 1:24 a.m. Friday, directly in front of Restaurante Flamas.
The man was described as stable. The page has no video and no scene photo — only a generic file photo of an ambulance.

timeline.text: Police had no information on any suspect; case referred to CIC Aguadilla.
body: The bullet entered and exited the abdomen; his condition was described as stable.
District agent Edwin Echevarría took the initial report and referred the case to the Criminal Investigations Corps (CIC) in Aguadilla. There was no information on a suspect.

items.title: LUMA work may cut power today on Calle Caney
items.summary: LUMA is installing automated equipment on Calle Caney as part of substation work across 17 towns before Thanksgiving. Brief outages are possible.
body: LUMA Energy scheduled restoration and modernization work at substations in 17 municipalities on the day before Thanksgiving.
In Rincón, crews are installing automated devices on Calle Caney. LUMA says the work could cause interruptions but didn't publish exact hours, so plan for a possible outage during the day.

items.title: “Del Campo al Mar” tasting dinner at Alma
items.summary: Chefs Vivoni Ventura and Brenda Gil Enseñat teamed up for a sunset tasting menu with cocktails at Alma Dynamic World Cuisine.
body: The dinner split the menu between land and sea: Ventura took the farm ingredients and Gil Enseñat the seafood, and they said every dish was a collaboration.
Highlights included cacao-crusted lamb chops with mushroom chimichurri, bok choy and cassava, and river shrimp over pumpkin polenta with a spicy mango glaze. Each course came with a matched cocktail.
Guests watched the sunset over the Tres Palmas Marine Reserve, and the evening included a traditional bomba performance. No date for another edition was announced.

image.alt: Del Campo al Mar dinner at Alma, Rincón

items.title: Flood advisory for Rincón, Aguada and Añasco
items.summary: The National Weather Service warned of urban and small-stream flooding after up to 1.5 inches of rain fell in the afternoon.
body: Doppler radar picked up heavy showers and thunderstorms over the west on Monday afternoon. By 3:07 p.m., up to an inch and a half had fallen in Rincón, Aguada and Añasco.

Forecasters warned of flooding in low-lying streets, spots with poor drainage, and normally dry creeks that can rise quickly. The advice: don't drive through flooded roads even if the water looks shallow, and take another route.

items.title: Hooded man enters home and shoots resident
items.summary: Heriberto Rosario, 56, was shot in the left arm Monday night at his home on Calle José Celso Barbosa. He is stable. CIC Aguadilla is investigating.
body: Rosario told police that someone dressed in black with a hood walked into his house and fired several shots without saying a word. One bullet hit his left arm.

He was taken to Hospital Buen Samaritano and then referred to a metro-area hospital. Agent Luis Sein Egipciaco of the Aguadilla Homicide Division is leading the case. The shooter has not been identified, and police describe the details as preliminary.
Different street from the Flamas shooting; police haven't linked the two.

items.title: $85M+ airport terminal contract awaits Fiscal Board
items.summary: The BQN terminal project would add four jet bridges so passengers board without walking outside. Approval from the Oversight Board is pending.
body: The Ports Authority's executive director said the new terminal contract is waiting on the Financial Oversight Board. It would add four jet bridges so passengers no longer walk across the tarmac in the rain.
Overall, more than $450 million in work is planned, including a runway renovation and a new taxiway. A new control tower and security cameras are already done.
He also said he expects new routes within two years, possibly including Germany, France and Italy. Airline negotiations run through the Puerto Rico Tourism Company.

items.title: Update: Man shot outside Restaurante Flamas has died
items.summary: Alejandro Chaparro Ruiz, 66, died of the gunshot wound after being moved to a metro-area hospital. Police now count the shooting as a murder.
body: Police listed the Flamas shooting in barrio Victoria among three murders reported over the Nov 20–22 weekend. Chaparro had been described as stable in the first reports.

He was treated first at Hospital Buen Samaritano in Aguadilla and then referred to a metro-area hospital, where he died. The CIC Aguadilla Homicide Division continues to investigate; no suspect, motive or arrest has been made public.

items.title: Man, 66, shot outside Restaurante Flamas
items.summary: Alejandro Chaparro Ruiz of Aguada was shot in the abdomen around 1:24 a.m. He later died at Centro Médico; police now classify it as a murder.
body: A 9-1-1 caller reported a person lying on the pavement in front of Restaurante Flamas. Officers found Chaparro with a gunshot wound to the abdomen.

He was treated at Hospital Buen Samaritano and referred to a San Juan–area hospital. The CIC Aguadilla Homicide Division is investigating. The full timeline is in the case tracker at the top of the app.

updates.text: Chaparro died of his wound at a San Juan–area hospital; police now list the case as a murder.

items.title: Avelo's new BQN flights are now running
items.summary: Twice-weekly nonstops from Lakeland/Orlando and New Haven, Connecticut began Nov 18 and 19.
body: Avelo Airlines added two nonstop routes into Rafael Hernández airport: Lakeland/Orlando starting Nov 18 and Tweed-New Haven starting Nov 19, each twice a week.
The Tourism Company estimated the routes' economic impact for the west coast at about $13.8 million.

items.title: Pole work in Urb. San Cristóbal
items.summary: LUMA crews are working on poles on San Cristóbal, Ermita, San Francisco, Narciso and 2 streets. Outages are possible.
body: Part of LUMA's pre-Thanksgiving round of substation and line work across 17 towns.
Streets listed: San Cristóbal, Ermita, San Francisco, Narciso and Calle 2. LUMA didn't post hours.

items.title: Pole-resilience work in Parcelas Tablonal
items.summary: LUMA scheduled pole hardening from 7 a.m. to 6 p.m.
body: LUMA's planned-improvements list showed pole-resilience work in Parcelas Tablonal for a full workday. More Aguada work was listed for the following days.

items.title: Flood advisory for Aguada, Añasco and Moca
items.summary: Heavy afternoon storms dropped 1 to 1.5 inches of rain. The advisory ran until 5 p.m.
body: The National Weather Service issued the advisory Thursday afternoon after strong showers. Ceiba, Gurabo, Juncos and Las Piedras were also under an advisory in the east.
Drivers were urged not to cross flooded roads.

items.title: Free Christmas season in the plaza through mid-January
items.summary: Family movies, Saturday artisan nights with live music, snow machines and a kids' train in Plaza José Adolfo Pesante. All free.
body: Thursday, Friday and Sunday: kids' movies. Saturday: Noches de Artesanías with local artisans and live music. Thursday through Sunday: the kids' train around the town center plus three artificial-snow stations and photo spots.

A free Thanksgiving lunch (600 plates) was served Nov 24. The season continues with a Fiesta de Reyes on Jan 6 and closes with the Fiestas de Pueblo, Jan 15–17. Announced by Mayor Kabir Solares García.

items.title: One of Mayagüez's 10 most wanted arrested in Cayey
items.summary: Jesús Alvarado Mercado, 23, wanted on weapons charges with $120,000 bail, was caught with help from the U.S. Marshals.
body: The Mayagüez Area Arrest Division picked him up in Cayey in a joint operation with the U.S. Marshals. The warrant stems from events on Dec 14, 2025, and covers illegal possession of a long gun or sawed-off shotgun and of ammunition.
He couldn't post bail and was sent to a correctional facility until his preliminary hearing.

items.title: Man dies after being pinned by vehicle at gas station
items.summary: Reported by El Vocero's crime desk.
body: Only the headline was available; El Vocero's full report has the details.

items.title: Man found shot in vacant lot near Candelaria
items.summary: The unidentified man was found between residencial Candelaria and the PR-2 footbridge. CIC Mayagüez is investigating.
body: A 9-1-1 call reported a body in a vacant lot. Officers found a man with gunshot wounds to several parts of his body.
Police didn't know who he was or what happened. The CIC Mayagüez Homicide Division and the on-duty prosecutor are handling it.

items.title: Charge filed in Barrio Sábalos body case
items.summary: Steven Fuster Santana, 41, faces a destruction-of-evidence charge for allegedly hiding the body of Mariel Patricia Crespo Cortés. Bail was set at $30,000.
body: Prosecutors say that on Nov 2 he wrapped the body of the 33-year-old woman in a sheet and hid it in a wooded area behind his home in barrio Sábalos.
He was identified in a lineup at the Mayagüez police headquarters. His preliminary hearing was set for Nov 17.

items.title: Afternoon storms and high tides, then drier for Thanksgiving
items.summary: Rincón was on the National Weather Service's list of western towns with an elevated flood risk Tuesday as afternoon storms hit the west. Tides ran above normal, and drier air arrives Wednesday into Thanksgiving.
body: The National Weather Service expected isolated afternoon showers and thunderstorms over the interior, west and northwest, with locally heavy rain, lightning and gusty winds. Rincón, Aguada, Aguadilla, Añasco and Mayagüez were all listed with an elevated flood risk.

Tides were expected to run above normal, which can cause minor flooding in low-lying coastal spots around high tide. Rough surf with breakers over six feet and a higher rip-current risk covered the north coast from Aguadilla east.
Forecasters expect showers to taper off Wednesday and Thursday as drier, more stable air moves in.

items.title: Caribbean Journal pitches Rincón as a weekend escape from San Juan
items.summary: A new travel feature tells visitors to skip the capital and spend about three nights in Rincón for surf, small oceanfront inns and sunset drinks.
body: The Caribbean Journal piece frames Rincón as a destination on its own rather than a day trip, and suggests flying into Aguadilla to reach the west coast sooner, with a rental car for getting around.

It matches beaches to conditions: watching surf from Domes near the Punta Higüero lighthouse, snorkeling at Steps in the Tres Palmas reserve on calm days, and the public balneario when swells are up. Sandy Beach is suggested for lunch, and the plaza's Thursday evening Art Walk gets a mention.
Places to stay and drink named in the story include Tamboo and Casa Isleña near Sandy Beach, and Villa Cofresí for its coconut rum cocktail.

items.title: Flood advisory for Mayagüez, Añasco and four mountain towns
items.summary: The National Weather Service warned of urban and small-stream flooding Monday afternoon after radar estimated 1 to 2.5 inches of rain. The advisory ran until 6 p.m.
facts: Añasco, Lares, Las Marías, Maricao, San Sebastián
body: Doppler radar showed 1 to 2.5 inches of rain had already fallen over parts of the western interior and coast, with another 1 to 2 inches possible, so the hardest-hit spots could see 2 to 4.5 inches in total.

Forecasters warned of flooding on streets with poor drainage and of small creeks and normally dry channels rising fast. The advice was the usual: don't drive into flooded roads, since most flood deaths happen in vehicles, and report flooding when it's safe to do so.

items.title: High rip-current risk from Aguadilla east; hot, mostly dry Thanksgiving
items.summary: The National Weather Service kept a high rip-current risk for north-coast beaches from Aguadilla to Fajardo heading into Thanksgiving. Heat index values could top 100°F Thursday, with more showers Friday, mainly in the west.
body: Forecasters warned that the calm, sunny weather could tempt people into the water even though rip currents along the north coast are strong enough to pull experienced swimmers out.

Thursday should be mostly dry and stable, with only a few short afternoon showers. Heat is the bigger concern: heat index values could pass 100°F in coastal and urban areas on Thanksgiving and Friday.
Friday brings a better chance of showers and some urban and small-stream flooding, mainly over western Puerto Rico.

earth.title: El Niño keeps strengthening toward a historic event
earth.summary: NOAA says a strong-to-very-strong El Niño is likely through January–March 2027, possibly one of the strongest on record since 1950.
body: In its Nov 12 update, NOAA's Climate Prediction Center kept its El Niño Advisory in place and said the event is still strengthening, with a strong-to-very-strong El Niño likely through January–March 2027.
Sea-surface temperatures in the key Niño 3.4 region were about 2.5°C above normal, and about 4.4°C above normal off South America. NOAA's next update is Dec 10.

earth.title: M4.4 quake near Mona Island felt in Puerto Rico
earth.summary: A deep quake about 65 miles northwest of Mona Island was felt across Puerto Rico. No tsunami warning, advisory or watch was issued.
body: The quake struck Saturday morning about 65 miles northwest of Mona Island at a depth of roughly 106 km, between eastern Dominican Republic and Puerto Rico's west coast.
Some reports describe two back-to-back quakes in the 4.6–4.7 range in the same area. Officials said there was no tsunami threat for Puerto Rico or the Virgin Islands.

luma.headline: No outage reported
luma.detail: No outage or load-shedding reports found for Rincón's pueblo area. LUMA had scheduled equipment work on Calle Caney in Rincón for Nov 25, which could cause brief interruptions.

updates.text: LUMA listed installation of automated equipment on Calle Caney in Rincón for today; brief interruptions possible.

claro.headline: No outage reported
claro.detail: No reports of Claro internet, mobile or TV problems in Rincón or western Puerto Rico.
